Donald Trump’s 56th TIME cover puts him ahead of Richard Nixon’s decades-old record

US President Donald Trump first appeared on TIME’s cover in 1989, when he was known mainly as a New York property developer and businessman.

Sakshi Mehra

02 October, 2026 04:38 pm IST

New Delhi: US President Donald Trump has spent decades wanting to be seen. Now, TIME has put a number on just how often it has chosen to show him: 56 times, more than anyone else in the magazine’s history.

His latest cover takes him past 37th US President Richard Nixon, who held the record with 55 covers for more than 50 years.

In 2017, shortly after taking office, he claimed he had appeared on TIME “like 14 or 15 times,” suggesting he had already set its record. In reality, he had appeared on 11 covers by 20 January that year, including eight in 2016.

Show Full Article

“I think we have the all-time record in the history of TIME magazine. If Tom Brady is on the cover, it’s one time because you won the Super Bowl or something, right? I’ve been on the cover 15 times this year. I don’t think that’s a record that could ever be broken,” Trump said at the time.

The record is now real.

TIME Editor-in-Chief Sam Jacobs said the 56th cover “marks a milestone for this magazine and for the President.” In the interview, Trump spoke about the Iran war, the economy, AI, renovations at the White House and his tense relationship with the press.

From tycoon to president  Trump first appeared on the TIME cover in January 1989, years before he entered politics. At the time, he was known mainly as a New York property developer and businessman. The cover reflected the attention around his wealth and celebrity.

“I have an absolute strategy, but it’s an innate strategy and not definable,” Trump told TIME for that first cover story. “When you start studying yourself too deeply, you start seeing things that maybe you don’t want to see.”

For years, Trump appeared on the cover only occasionally. That changed with his 2015 presidential campaign. TIME then followed his rise from TV celebrity and businessman to presidential candidate, president, his impeachments, legal battles and the events of 6 January 2021.

Trump returned to the TIME cover after leaving office. The magazine covered his political comeback in 2024, when he won the presidency again. Its latest cover comes as he heads toward the 2026 midterm elections.

Trump has also kept an eye on his TIME covers. During a 2025 visit to Israel, he was given a framed collection of his earlier covers.

“Wow, I love it,” he said . “I want to make sure it comes back with us.”

Trump told TIME during his latest interview that he had liked only 17 of his previous 55 covers. Fake TIME covers featuring him have also appeared at his private clubs over the years, including one that the magazine itself identified as bogus.

‘President-press relationship inherently adversarial’ Eight of the 10 people who have appeared most often on the TIME cover are US presidents. Trump, Nixon and Ronald Reagan are at the top, followed by presidents, including Bill Clinton, Barack Obama,  George W Bush and Jimmy Carter. Jesus is also among the most frequent subjects.

Nixon’s 55 covers came during a major period in US politics, including the Watergate scandal. He held the record for more than 50 years. TIME has also drawn a parallel between Nixon and Trump over their tense relationships with the press.

“The relationship between Presidents and the press is inherently adversarial,” historian David Greenberg wrote in TIME . “Since the emergence of a modern mass media and a professional White House press corps in the early 20th century, Presidents have sought to use journalists to disseminate their ideas, goals, and achievements and have treated coverage that deviates from their spin as misleading, hostile, or malicious.”

The tension is visible in Trump’s latest interview too. The interview came days after his administration had attempted to restrict access for some journalists, while Trump continued to accuse news organisations of unfair coverage.

(Edited by Saptak Datta)
